2607.29240.title: When Model Priors Conflict with Visual Evidence: Mitigating Commonsense-Driven Hallucinations by Selective Prior Calibration
2607.29240.paper_summary: In vision--language models, commonsense-driven hallucination (CDH) occurs when a model's commonsense prior overrides clear visual evidence of an atypical state. For example, a model may report that a visibly six-fingered hand has five fingers. We show that these errors are systematically directed: when a model answers a question about a counterfactual (CF) image incorrectly, its answer often coincides with the candidate it prefers without access to the image. Suppressing this prior indiscriminately can repair CF errors, but may also disrupt correct answers on matched commonsense (CS) images, where the same prior is helpful. We therefore propose Selective Prior Calibration (SPC), which subtracts candidate-level prior-preference estimates from image-conditioned scores with an instance-dependent strength and revises the original prediction only when the resulting score pattern strongly supports an alternative. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SPC substantially improves accuracy on CF images while largely preserving accuracy on matched CS images. Furthermore, these gains generalize across CDH categories, candidate-answer permutations, and other conflict benchmarks, while SPC rarely alters predictions on benchmarks without such conflicts.
2607.29240.paper_summary_zh: 在視覺-語言模型中，常識驅動的幻覺（CDH）發生在模型的常識先驗超越了對非典型狀態的明確視覺證據時。<lb/>例如，模型可能報告一隻明顯有六根手指的手只有五根手指。<lb/>我們顯示這些錯誤是系統性導向的：當模型對一幅反事實（CF）圖像的問題回答錯誤時，它的答案往往與它在沒有訪問圖像的情況下偏好的候選答案一致。<lb/>無差別地抑制這一先驗可以修復CF錯誤，但也可能擾亂在匹配常識（CS）圖像上的正確答案，在這種情況下，相同的先驗是有幫助的。<lb/>因此，我們提出了選擇性先驗校準（SPC），它根據實例依賴的強度從圖像條件的分數中減去候選級別的先驗偏好估計，並僅在結果分數模式強烈支持替代方案時修正原始預測。<lb/>大量實驗表明，SPC顯著提高了CF圖像的準確性，同時在匹配的CS圖像上基本保持了準確性。<lb/>此外，這些增益在CDH類別、候選答案排列和其他衝突基準中具有普遍性，而SPC在沒有這種衝突的基準上很少改變預測。
